correctness.rationale: The adjacent-support-line intersection lengths give the exact halfplane-polygon area. Averaging a uniform normal-angle phase replaces cyclic samples by the exact support autocorrelation; its Fourier diagonalization is algebraically exact for every n. An even Taylor expansion of a C^8 autocorrelation and integration by parts yield the second- and fourth-order curvature-radius invariants with sixth-order remainder. The harmonic family has positive curvature radius for every m>=2 and an explicit sign threshold; independent shoelace computations agree.

value.rationale: For natural equiangular tangent approximations, the leading area defect depends only on the mean-square curvature radius while the fourth-order correction additionally measures its angular gradient. Isoperimetric families with identical normal-angle curvature-radius histograms have opposite correction signs, demonstrating new geometric information and providing an exact finite-size Fourier benchmark for tangent-normal discretization.
